title: Giving
hookLine: Catholics support the Church and the poor from what they have
tomorrow: why does owing weigh so much, even when the number is small?

cards: The first paycheck lands, and before the excitement wears off, the math starts: phone bill, gas, savings, the thing waiting in the cart. The Bible's old answer to how much to give has a name.
In Genesis, Abram gives the priest Melchisedech a tenth of everything. Later, the law of Moses calls that tenth of the harvest a tithe and says it is holy to the Lord.

teach.h: NO FIXED NUMBER IN THE PRECEPT.
teach.b: So does the Church require exactly a tenth? Not by its own law. Among the precepts of the Church, the Catechism lists helping to provide for the Church's needs, each according to their own ability.
No fixed number. What scripture keeps coming back to is the order.

teach.h: THE FIRST OF ALL THY FRUITS.
teach.b: Proverbs, in the Douay-Rheims: "Honour the Lord with thy substance, and give him of the first of all thy fruits." The first, not the leftovers.
And the spirit of it: Paul tells the Corinthians that each should give as they've decided in their heart, not sadly or because they have to, "for God loveth a cheerful giver."
Now look back over two weeks.
A road walked with eyes up, a first task offered, a noon pause, a slump outlasted, a door, a table, a look back at night, a day handed over.
Then work as creation, work done well, colleagues, both sides of the deal, and worth that isn't a job. Giving is where it all comes back around: what the work earned, offered first.

how: Catholics support their parish through the Sunday collection or a regular pledge and give to the poor through parish and diocesan charities; the Church's precept leaves the amount to each person's means.

o: a share given first, traditionally a tenth
a fee once paid to rent a pew at church
a tax the government collects for churches

games.q: your cousin wants to give part of every paycheck but spends it all by Tuesday every time. by Proverbs, what helps?
o: set the giving aside first, the day the money arrives.
give whatever is left at the end of the month.
wait until the amount is big enough to matter.
games.why: Proverbs says give of the first of all thy fruits. the order does the work: first, not leftovers.

practice: Pick an amount that's honest for you, any amount, and decide where it will go: your parish, a food pantry, someone you know who's in need. Write it down with the day you'll give it, and put it above every other line in your budget.

wordCard.voice: Tithe. In the Bible, the tenth set aside as holy; in Catholic practice, a share given first, by each one's means.

orig.note: Latin: a tenth, the Vulgate's word for the tithe.

carryVoice: Your line: give first, from the top and gladly, before the bills. Two weeks of ordinary holiness, done.
